text:
1. A principle holds even in stories that depart from the known world.
2. Stories may include ghosts walking battlements.
3. Stories may include witches meeting on a heath.
4. Characters who encounter supernatural beings talk as frightened, doubtful, or ambitious men ordinarily talk.
5. In such stories, the action rises above ordinary life.
6. In such stories, the dialogue remains at the level of ordinary life.
7. Horatio, confronted with the Ghost, does not declaim.
8. Horatio asks the Ghost plainly what it is.
9. Horatio asks the Ghost plainly why it has come.
10. Horatio's response to the Ghost resembles how an ordinary person would respond.
